about.title: South Pasadena Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a preventable collision changes everything, and South Pasadena's quiet, tree-lined streets don't make that loss any easier to carry. Local crash data shows dozens of injury collisions each year along corridors like Huntington Drive and Monterey Road, and while South Pasadena's most recent recorded year showed no traffic deaths, fatal crashes still happen on the roads that connect this city to greater Los Angeles County. California law gives certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to pursue a wrongful death claim, but that right comes with a strict two-year deadline from the date of death, and even less time if a government entity is involved. Our team handles wrongful death claims across Los Angeles County. We can explain your options, review the circumstances, and help pursue the compensation the law allows. There's no cost to you unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why South Pasadena Families Choose Us

items.title: Standing Matters, and Time Is Limited
items.desc: California law restricts who can file a wrongful death claim, typically starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and the filing window is generally two years from the date of death. We can quickly assess who qualifies and confirm the applicable deadline before it passes.

items.title: Claims Against Government Entities Move Faster
items.desc: If a South Pasadena roadway or a public agency is involved, the deadline to act shrinks considerably compared to a standard two-year window. Getting legal guidance early helps ensure notice requirements aren't missed.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: California law allows families to seek compensation for funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of companionship and guidance, not just economic damages. We can help identify every loss the law recognizes in your family's situation.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children to bring the claim. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing under certain conditions. We can review your family's specific situation to confirm who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in South Pasadena?
items.answer: In most cases, California law allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. That window shortens significantly if a government entity, such as one responsible for a road like Fair Oaks Avenue or Monterey Road, may be involved. Because deadlines vary by circumstance, it's worth getting legal guidance sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, they are separate matters. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action a family brings to recover their own losses. One can proceed regardless of the outcome of the other.
